key_concepts: Rotation is Earth spinning on its axis; revolution is Earth orbiting the Sun
Earth revolves around the Sun from west to east in a counterclockwise direction
Earth's orbit is an ellipse, so its distance from the Sun changes during the year
Perihelion is Earth's closest point to the Sun; aphelion is its farthest point
The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun receives more sunlight hours and more direct radiatio
Longer daytime and more direct sunlight make summer warmer than winter
Solstices occur when Earth's tilt toward or away from the Sun is at its maximum
Equinoxes bring nearly equal day and night lengths
Summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs around June 21 or 22
Winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs around December 21 or 22
Vernal equinox occurs around March 20 or 21 and autumnal equinox around September 22 or 23
